items.name: E1_snake_charmer
items.text: Instantly recognizable stereotypical 'ancient Egypt' music as heard in cartoons and adventure films: a nasal, buzzy snake-charmer mizmar / zurna melody that leans hard on the Hijaz scale's signature step (D, E-flat, F-sharp, G, A, B-flat, C), with sinuous ornaments and trills; belly-dance darbuka groove (doum-tek baladi rhythm) loud in the mix, finger cymbals (zills) and tambourine, oud strumming, 120 BPM. Exotic, sly, catchy, bazaar and pyramids feeling. Instrumental, no vocals.

items.name: E2_epic_pharaoh
items.text: Epic Hollywood ancient Egypt adventure score: full orchestra playing sweeping Hijaz-scale string runs with the augmented second clearly heard, deep low male choir chanting 'ah', huge war drums and taiko hits, brass stabs, and a soaring female wordless Middle-Eastern vocal melisma with ululation-like ornaments over the top; pyramids, pharaohs and gods, majestic and mysterious, 100 BPM.

items.name: E3_tomb_mystic
items.text: Mysterious ancient Egyptian tomb music: an ethereal female voice singing a wordless Arabic-style melisma in the Hijaz scale with heavy ornamentation, oud tremolo, a low drone, a slow darbuka pattern, sistrum and finger cymbal shimmers, deep temple reverb; dark, sacred, mystical, unmistakably 'Egypt'.

items.name: E4_playful_egypt
items.text: Playful, comedic stereotypical Egyptian cartoon music: a sneaky clarinet and mizmar melody in the Hijaz scale (snake-charmer style), bouncy pizzicato strings, darbuka and riq groove with finger cymbals, little oud flourishes, 115 BPM; cheeky and fun, like a cartoon character tiptoeing past the pyramids. Instrumental.
